text:
jon-acme: Hey team — we've been seeing a spike in 200-OK responses with 300-400ms extra RTT for EU users. Dug into logs and a bunch of requests are hitting us-west edge instead of eu-west. Not sure why, nothing changed on our side.

maria-support: Sorry about that, can you paste the raw request headers (sanitized) and a sample request-id? Also which SDK + version are you using?

jon-acme: We're on company-sdk-js v2.4.1. Sample request-id: req_0a9f3b2c. Raw headers (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
X-Client-Region: eu;;,west
Region: eu; ,west
User-Agent: acme-service/1.2.3
```

Looks like the client SDK builds the Region header from a config array and sometimes concatenates using both semicolons and commas (legacy and new code paths).

maria-support: Huh. That's... messy. Can you confirm whether the SDK sets both X-Client-Region and Region? That mixed delimiter string stands out ("eu;;,west").

jon-acme: Yeah, we set both for backwards compatibility. We didn't realize the string could contain consecutive delimiters and empty tokens. Repro steps:
1) config.regions = ["eu", "", "west"]
2) SDK does regions.join(';') then legacy middleware appends ',west' -> result ends up with multi-delimiters.

kevin-eng: @maria-support tagging infra — router normalizes region headers but we recently changed the delimiter precedence to prefer semicolon-separated tokens for legacy reasons. If the first token is empty, router falls back to nearest edge (us-west) — that matches the symptom.

maria-support: @jon-acme thanks, that explains the misroute. For immediate mitigation can you remove the Region header or set it explicitly to a single value (e.g., "eu-west") in your proxy? That should route correctly.

jon-acme: Can do. Any longer-term fix on Redwood side?

kevin-eng: Yes — ops-oncall and I looked at router logic. Router currently does: `split(header, /[,;])/` then picks tokens[0] without trimming empties. Two issues: mixed delimiters and empty-token handling. Proposed fix: normalize delimiters to commas, filter empty/whitespace tokens, then validate against allowed region list. I'll open a PR to change parser to: `header.split(/[,;\s]+/).filter(Boolean)` and canonicalize to region codes like `eu-west`.

ops-oncall: I'll roll a canary of the fix in eu region first. Plan: deploy to canary in 30m, monitor routing and latency for 1h, then promote. If we see no regressions, prod rollout in 3h. ETA for full fix: ~4h including rollout + monitoring.

router-bot: ROUTER-INVESTIGATION req_0a9f3b2c: matched route rule R-CLIENT-REGION (priority 200). Parsed tokens: ["", "", "west"]. Selected token index 0 -> empty -> fallback to nearest-pop (us-west).

maria-support: Adding this to the escalation so account team sees the plan. Suggestion for customers in the meantime: set explicit query param `?region=eu-west` or remove header as @maria-support suggested.

jon-acme: Removing the Region header from our ingress proxy now. I'll report back if things improve. Thanks for quick triage. :pray:

kevin-eng: Also adding a regression test to the router suite: inputs with mixed delimiters and empty tokens should not prefer empty first token.

ops-oncall: Deployed canary patch (router parser) to eu-canary. Initial checks show requests with mixed delimiters now normalize to ["eu", "west"] and choose eu as expected. Rolling to prod in 2h unless anomalies.

jon-acme: Confirmed — latency for eu users back to baseline after header removal. Thanks everyone.

maria-support: Glad that helped. Will keep this thread updated with the PR/CHANGES link when Kevin posts it.

kevin-eng: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/router/merge_requests/482 (will add finer-grained unit tests).

jon-acme: Cheers, leaving this open until prod rollout completes.

maria-support: Closing loop once ops confirms full rollout. :white_check_mark:
